A better first bench.

Choose a kit that fits your table, your hands, and the flies you want to tie. Skip the box of materials you will never use.

Quick answer

Wapsi Starter Kit is my pick for a complete first kit. It includes tools, materials, and a handbook for ten trout patterns. Choose it if those patterns match the flies you want to tie.[1]

02

Try the vise before you commit

  1. 01

    Bring your hook sizes

    Test the smallest and largest hooks you expect to use. The hook must stay put without excessive force.

  2. 02

    Match the base to your table

    Check the table edge for a clamp. Check a pedestal for stability on the surface you will use.

  3. 03

    Sit in your normal position

    Reach the hook and controls without hunching. Confirm that the setup suits your dominant hand.

  4. 04

    Count what is missing

    List the bobbin, scissors, finishing tool, hooks, thread, and pattern materials before you compare totals.

04

Buy the recipe, not the wall

What works well

  • One packet can serve several flies in the same pattern.
  • A focused kit keeps the first bench session simple.
  • A few familiar materials make mistakes easier to spot.

The trade-offs

  • A large assortment can include hook sizes you will not use.
  • A vise-only price leaves out the rest of the bench.
  • A tool upgrade does not replace practice.
05

Keep the grip. Protect the edges.

  • ✓Clean loose fibers and adhesive from the bench after each session.
  • ✓Keep the vise and tools dry.
  • ✓Use the maker’s method for jaw adjustment and lubrication.
  • ✓Reserve fine scissors for soft materials.
  • ✓Store hooks and spare jaws in labelled containers.
A warranty has a scope

PEAK’s statement covers defects in material or workmanship. Read the current terms before you treat damage or wear as a warranty claim.

[3]
A few good questions

Before you head out

Is a starter kit a false economy?

Only if the tools or patterns do not suit you. Check the contents against your first two or three recipes.

Which vise feature matters most?

A stable grip on your hooks, with room for your hands. Test that before you compare extra features.

Should I buy several scissors?

Start with one good pair for thread and soft materials. Use a separate suitable cutter for wire.
